engineManufacturers.name: Mercedes FO 110D
engineManufacturers.desc: The benchmark hybrid architecture. Exceptional ERS and top-end power.

engineManufacturers.name: Ferrari Tipo 046
engineManufacturers.desc: Raw power leader. Slightly less refined ERS than the silver works engine but devastating on power tracks.

engineManufacturers.name: Mugen-Honda MF-301HA
engineManufacturers.desc: Exclusive works deal with the British racing-green outfit. Strong hybrid efficiency and compact packaging.

engineManufacturers.name: Peugeot A12
engineManufacturers.desc: A new works powertrain programme with external manufacturer support. High-upside engine for Milton Keynes Racing and Toro GP.

engineManufacturers.name: Ford JD Zetec-R
engineManufacturers.desc: New entrant. Behind now but aggressive development trajectory — could be a dark horse by 2029.

td.name: Patrick Head
td.desc: The engineering backbone of Williams whose relentless pursuit of mechanical and aerodynamic excellence dominated the mid-90s.

td.name: John Barnard
td.desc: Renowned for working from his UK-based design office, he crafted the pioneering but complex F310 chassis for Ferrari before the Brawn era began.

td.name: Ross Brawn
td.desc: The mastermind behind Benettons title successes who optimized the B196 before planning his historic move to Maranello.

td.name: Neil Oatley
td.desc: A stable, pragmatic engineer who steady-shipped McLarens design department during their transition into the powerhouse Mercedes era.

td.name: Gary Anderson
td.desc: A highly resourceful designer capable of maximizing a mid-field budget to build stunning and competitive yellow cars.

td.name: Leo Ress
td.desc: The engineering anchor for Peter Sauber who specialized in constructing incredibly safe and structurally solid chassis.

td.name: Frank Dernie
td.desc: A veteran aerodynamicist who successfully adapted the JS43 to claim a shock victory in the chaotic, wet Monaco Grand Prix.

td.name: Harvey Postlethwaite
td.desc: An innovative technical visionary who frequently pioneered groundbreaking concepts despite Tyrrells severely limited financial backing.

td.name: Alan Jenkins
td.desc: Tasked with navigating the teams turbulent transition to Tom Walkinshaws ownership, he focused on building an aerodynamically predictable car.

td.name: Aldo Costa
td.desc: A young, brilliant Italian engineer cutting his teeth by squeezing maximum mechanical grip out of Minardi’s microscopic budget.

td.name: George Ryton
td.desc: Faced an impossible challenge with the cash-strapped squad, attempting to make the overweight FG03 meet the strict 107% qualifying rule.

rs.name: Dickie Stanford
rs.desc: A cool-headed operation manager who perfectly orchestrated Williams championship-winning multi-stop pit strategies.

rs.name: Luca Baldisserri
rs.desc: Handpicked to guide Michael Schumachers tactical decisions, he showed early signs of the operational genius that resurrected Ferrari.

rs.name: Pat Symonds
rs.desc: The undisputed king of the pit-lane chess board who famously pioneered multi-stop fuel strategies during F1’s refueling golden era.

rs.name: Martin Whitmarsh
rs.desc: A methodical operational leader who focused on calculated, low-risk strategies to ensure McLaren maximized points finishes.

rs.name: Tim Edwards
rs.desc: A sharp operational manager who loved to gamble on aggressive, high-reward strategies whenever rain disrupted the grid.

rs.name: Beat Zehnder
rs.desc: The ultimate midfield opportunist whose meticulous oversight ensured Sauber rarely wasted a tactical opening.

rs.name: Cesare Fiorio
rs.desc: A legendary master tactician who flawlessly timed Olivier Paniss wet-to-dry tire switch to win the historic 1996 Monaco GP.

rs.name: Steve Nielsen
rs.desc: A logistics and regulations expert who specialized in keeping Tyrrells race executions disciplined and mistake-free.

rs.name: Jackie Oliver
rs.desc: Utilized highly aggressive, low-fuel qualifying strategies to get the underpowered Arrows car as high up the grid as possible.

rs.name: John Walton
rs.desc: Forced to rely on long endurance strategies and attrition, hoping to steal a rare point when frontrunners broke down.

rs.name: Cesare Gariboldi
rs.desc: Strategy options were heavily restricted by a massive lack of pace, focusing purely on getting the cars out before the 107% cutoff.

cm.name: Carl Gaden
cm.desc: Commanded the Williams garage with military precision, keeping the FW18 incredibly reliable throughout the title fight.

cm.name: Nigel Stepney
cm.desc: A legendary figure in the garage who instilled a fierce work ethic that turned Ferraris mechanical reliability into a fortress.

cm.name: M. Cowlishaw
cm.desc: A veteran mechanic who kept the temperamental B196 chassis properly tuned to match Alesi and Bergers contrasting styles.

cm.name: Gerry Convy
cm.desc: Maintained an immaculate, hyper-organized garage workspace that mirrored Ron Denniss strict perfectionist philosophies.

cm.name: Dino Moscardi
cm.desc: Led a passionate crew that regularly pulled off overnight miracles to repair heavily damaged cars on a tight schedule.

cm.name: Urs Kuratle
cm.desc: Provided exceptional Swiss efficiency to ensure the Ford-powered Sauber cars were flawlessly assembled every weekend.

cm.name: Gilles Alegoet
cm.desc: Managed a highly skilled French crew capable of keeping the intricate Mugen-Honda V10 running perfectly under high pressure.

cm.name: Roger Hill
cm.desc: A loyal Tyrrell stalwart who relied on decades of experience to keep old equipment performing at its absolute mechanical limit.

cm.name: Dave Luckett
cm.desc: An experienced technician who held the garage together amidst massive ownership shakeups and structural changes during the year.

cm.name: Paolo Brandi
cm.desc: Squeezed every ounce of life out of recycled customer parts through pure Italian passion and mechanical resourcefulness.

cm.name: Alan Mugglestone
cm.desc: Battled severe parts shortages and financial chaos just to assemble two legal cars before the pit lane opened.

pcc.name: J. Williams
pcc.desc: Orchestrated one of the sharpest refueling and tire-change crews of the 90s, rarely costing Hill or Villeneuve time.

pcc.name: Bino Baldini
pcc.desc: Infamous for his intense drill-sergeant approach that drastically reduced Ferraris average refueling pit-stop times.

pcc.name: Joan Villadelprat
pcc.desc: Set the golden standard for rapid refueling stops back in 1994 and maintained that lightning-fast execution through 1996.

pcc.name: Dave Ryan
pcc.desc: A hard-nosed disciplinarian who ensured McLarens pit lane operations were executed with clinical, risk-averse precision.

pcc.name: Andy Stevenson
pcc.desc: A rising talent in the pit lane who motivated his young crew to regularly beat top-tier factory teams in raw stop speed.

pcc.name: Jacky Eeckelaert
pcc.desc: Kept his crew highly calm and methodical, prioritizing error-free tire swaps over dangerous, fractions-of-a-second gambles.

pcc.name: R. Chinchero
pcc.desc: Drilled a cohesive crew that executed a flawless, pressure-filled stop for Panis during his miraculous run to victory in Monaco.

pcc.name: Bob Mills
pcc.desc: Kept an aging, unglamorous pit crew working in perfect harmony to ensure no avoidable mistakes occurred during stops.

pcc.name: John Wickham
pcc.desc: Successfully kept morale high among the tire changers despite the team facing intense off-track financial uncertainty.

pcc.name: Luigi Montanini
pcc.desc: Compensated for a lack of automated pit equipment with incredibly synchronized, high-effort manual teamwork.

pcc.name: Daniele Forti
pcc.desc: Pit operations were frequently chaotic and unpracticed due to the team’s frantic, short-lived weekend schedules.
